# 12 — Dependency inventory

*Derived from `gateway/Cargo.toml`, `gateway/Cargo.lock`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`.*

Requirement, resolved version, and the rationale the manifest itself records. A blank reason means the manifest gives none.

## Rust (`gateway/`)

| Crate | Group | Requirement | Resolved | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `axum` | dependencies | `0.8` | `0.8.9` |  |
| `moka` | dependencies | `0.12` | `0.12.16` |  |
| `opentelemetry` | dependencies | `0.27` | `0.27.1` | OTLP over HTTP rather than gRPC: reqwest is already here, and the gRPC stack would add tonic and prost to a build that has to fit a 2 GB jail. |
| `opentelemetry-otlp` | dependencies | `0.27` | `0.27.0` |  |
| `opentelemetry_sdk` | dependencies | `0.27` | `0.27.1` |  |
| `prometheus` | dependencies | `0.13` | `0.13.4` | Exposition format, histogram bucketing and label handling are not worth hand-rolling, and the text format is a contract scrapers depend on. `process` adds the standard process_* collectors (CPU, RSS, open FDs, start time) that prometheus_client registered by default and whose absence blanked any dashboard reading process_resident_memory_bytes. The feature is inert off Linux -- both its procfs dependency and the collector module are target-gated -- so the FreeBSD jail still reports no process_* series. See metrics.rs. |
| `redis` | dependencies | `0.27` | `0.27.6` | L2 cache. No TLS, matching the deployments: Redis is reached over the jail's loopback or the compose network, never across the internet. connection-manager gives a single multiplexed, self-reconnecting connection. Without it every get and set opened a fresh TCP connection, so an L1 miss cost a connect and an unreachable Redis cost a full connect timeout per lookup -- where the Python client pooled from one `from_url` at construction. |
| `reqwest` | dependencies | `0.12` | `0.12.28` | No TLS: the gateway talks plain HTTP to osrm-routed, and dropping the TLS stack keeps the FreeBSD build honest about what is actually exercised. |
| `serde` | dependencies | `1` | `1.0.229` |  |
| `serde_json` | dependencies | `1` | `1.0.151` | raw_value lets the VRP solver embed the engine's route geometry verbatim instead of decoding and re-encoding its coordinates. preserve_order keeps object keys in insertion order, as a Python dict does. Without it every serde_json::Map came out key-sorted -- visible in `ctx`, in `/vrp/allocate`'s allocations, and in the graph edge attributes. The cache key is unaffected: it sorts through its own BTreeMap in cache.rs, deliberately. |
| `serde_path_to_error` | dependencies | `0.1` | `0.1.20` | Reports which field failed to deserialise, not just that something did. Without it every parse error lands on `body` with no path, and the path is what clients branch on. |
| `sha2` | dependencies | `0.10` | `0.10.9` |  |
| `tokio` | dependencies | `1` | `1.53.1` |  |
| `tower-http` | dependencies | `0.6` | `0.6.11` | catch-panic only. Starlette wrapped every request in ServerErrorMiddleware, so an unexpected exception became a 500; without an equivalent a panic here aborts the connection, the client sees a reset rather than a response, and the request is never counted -- the metrics go quiet exactly when they matter. |
| `tracing` | dependencies | `0.1` | `0.1.44` |  |
| `tracing-opentelemetry` | dependencies | `0.28` | `0.28.0` |  |
| `tracing-subscriber` | dependencies | `0.3` | `0.3.23` |  |
| `utoipa` | dependencies | `5` | `5.5.0` | Generates the OpenAPI document from the types that actually serve requests, which is what ends the dependency on FastAPI for the schema. |
| `tokio` | dev-dependencies | `1` | `1.53.1` |  |

## Python (tooling, tests, examples)

| `httpx` | dependencies | `httpx>=0.27.0` | `0.28.1` | The distribution is the `vrp` platform, because that is the part another repository can depend on. It was called `osrm-api-gateway` while nothing consumed it and the name cost nothing; shipping the routing platform under a name that says "gateway" would mislead every consumer, and renaming is free exactly once -- now, before anything pins it. The gateway itself is `gateway/`, a Rust binary, and is not a Python distribution at all. What `vrp/` imports at module level, and nothing else. `starlette` and `uvicorn` are here because `parity/engine.py` serves recorded fixtures and `T-102`'s successor hosts SDD 9.4 on them; `tests/test_packaging.py` keeps this list honest against the source rather than against memory. |
